title: Taking a Payment at the Desk Against a Granite Ridge Pass Account
content:
## When this facility applies

A household holding a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass that is financed over scheduled instalments may have money that has fallen due taken from them during a call. The collective takes it as one payment at the desk against that pass account. The figure presented is the amount fixed by the collective's basis for a pass account in arrears; the agent works it out from the records and the published terms and passes it in.

## The business effect

The payment is booked on the pass account as a cleared collection dated today, and the amount still to be collected on that pass record drops by the same figure, so the guest sees the arrears on their pass account fall the moment the call ends.

## How it is invoked

The agent unlocks the hidden agent tool `collect_past_due_0159c539` and then calls it. It is an agent-side tool and is not handed to the guest.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pass_id` | the reference number of the season pass record whose pass account the payment is taken against | an identifier, as returned by the season pass lookup |
| `presented_amount_usd` | the money taken in this single payment | a fixed-format figure in USD to 2 decimal places, never negative and never rounded to whole dollars; the collection is booked at exactly this figure |

Neither parameter carries an enumerated set of values.

## What comes back

A confirmation sentence carrying the new pass account entry reference, a string beginning `pcol_`, the pass record reference it was booked against, the amount collected in USD to 2 decimal places and the amount still to be collected on that pass account afterwards, also in USD to 2 decimal places. The presence of that entry reference is what indicates the payment was recorded.

## Contract questions

*Does the tool work the figure out?* No. It books the figure given, exactly as given.

*Is the figure rounded on the way in?* It is booked at exactly the figure passed, to 2 decimal places.

*What shows the payment landed?* The entry reference beginning `pcol_` in the sentence that comes back.
